A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same mechanistic-independence framework. Their complete main texts and appendices, including equations, proofs, figures, and results, support reliable comparison.

before.justification: Figure 1 and Appendix C report original autoencoder experiments across support-overlap levels, comprising 120 trained models.

after.justification: v2 retains the overlap experiments and adds original two-ball image experiments, quantitative results, reconstructions, and latent traversals in Appendix D.2.

M1.justification: The independence framework and original compositional-contrast training remain. Appendix D.2 adds an experimental autoencoder with separately parameterized additive slot decoders and MSE-only training, structurally enforcing Type H2 independence.

E1.justification: Beyond the retained invertible-MLP synthetic observations, v2 evaluates non-invertible generation of two-ball RGB images with position and color factors. This introduces image-domain disentanglement under permutation ambiguity. Occluded scenes are excluded from this experiment; their discussion is theoretical.

E2.justification: No competing-method baselines are added or removed. The original autoencoder configuration comparisons remain, and the new image experiment reports one additive autoencoder without comparative baseline results.

E3.justification: The new image experiment introduces a permutation-aware evaluation procedure: center-of-mass matching selects latent permutations before computing SIS*. It also specifies 300,000/10,000/50,000 training/validation/test images and a 1,000-epoch training protocol. The original overlap experiment's configuration grid and normalization remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix D.2 adds a focused diagnostic case study using individual-slot reconstructions and position/color traversals to examine factor separation and encoder discontinuities. The existing sensitivity analysis over support overlap is retained.

E5.justification: v1 already reports five seeds per overlap configuration. v2 additionally presents five-seed RMSE and SIS* summaries with ± values in Table 1, but does not identify the uncertainty statistic. This adds uncertainty reporting without establishing increased repetition of the original experiments.

E6.justification: The original overlap scatter plot and findings are retained. New Table 1 reports RMSE 1.30 ± 0.18 and SIS* 99.6 ± 0.05; Figures 4–6 add image reconstructions and evidence of a latent discontinuity despite accurate decoding. These are additional results under new conditions, not same-setting performance gains.

T1.justification: Theorem 1 strengthens path-connectedness to simple connectedness, explicitly requires continuity of the generator and a covering-map decoder, and receives a replacement lifting-based proof and relaxation conditions. Appendix A.2 revises the equivalence propositions and proofs. Appendix B adds a proof characterizing compositional-contrast minimizers for a constructed generator under a determinant constraint.

C1.justification: The abstract and contribution bullets retain the same central claims: distribution-independent mechanistic identifiability, multidimensional factors and non-invertible generators, a hierarchy of criteria, and graph-based characterization. The conclusion's emphasis on the coherence–interaction tradeoff restates an interpretation already present in v1.

C2.justification: New Section 4.3 explains criterion-specific limitations involving shadows, reflections, transparency, occlusion, and higher-order derivatives. Appendices C and D.2 expand the distinction between decoder identifiability and encoder ambiguity or discontinuity. Conversely, v1's specific discussion of compositional-contrast failure from a large shared Jacobian row is removed.

D1.justification: Appendix D.2 adds extensive reproducibility information: image construction and filtering, resolution and pixel range, dataset splits, the ResNet-18 encoder and additive subdecoder layers, and AdamW hyperparameters. The original synthetic experiment's details are retained in Appendix D.1; they are not replaced by these new settings.

R1.justification: The introduction expands its structural-identifiability taxonomy with citations including Jutten and Karhunen, Kivva et al., Lyu and Fu, and Nguyen and Fu. An AdamW reference is added and Reizinger et al. (2022) is removed. The central positioning relative to prior mechanistic-identifiability work remains.

P1.justification: v2 moves the overlap experiment into a dedicated Experiments section, adds a limitations subsection, reorganizes the appendices, and clarifies full versus partial disentanglement terminology. It also updates affiliations and publication headers. Much of the existing narrative remains unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adds Table 1 and Figures 4–6, introducing quantitative summaries, slot-reconstruction grids, latent-code curves, and traversal reconstructions. The original scatter plot is relocated with a revised caption and redrawn support schematic; the hierarchy and slice-connectedness diagrams are retained.

improvement.justification: v2 substantially improves the precision of the central global-identifiability argument through explicit lifting conditions, a rewritten proof, and revised equivalence assumptions. The new non-invertible image experiment and detailed applicability discussion provide support absent from v1's invertible-vector experiments. The guarantee is narrower, and Appendix C still does not verify all newly required lifting conditions, but the gains in theoretical qualification and empirical support are substantial.
